question.problem:
Compute $P(1<X<3)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8}({x}^{3}+x),\, & 0\le x\le 2, \\ \frac{1}{8}(x-2) & 2<x\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

current_example.problem:
Compute $P\left( 2 \leq          X \leq          4 \right)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14097680/assets/f973a91bef981994b15a29b0dc2d7635c041d2a9179d46a1e7f40210401bcb93.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a \leq        X \leq        b) = \int_a^b f(x) \, \textrm dx.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2\le X\le 4) & ={\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{1}{9}x\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{4}(x-3)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{18}{x}^{2}]}_{2}^{3}+{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-3x]}_{3}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}[{3}^{2}-{2}^{2}]+([\frac{1}{2}(4)^{2}-3(4)]-[\frac{1}{2}(3)^{2}-3(3)]) \\  & =\frac{5}{18}-4+\frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{14}{18} \\  & =\frac{7}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
